Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: list the unlinked active runs that scheduled close cleanup keeps

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-7856` @ `5f81d6c37591a2530fc31c58a81705cda885cc69` (integration branch metadata matches; mismatch `false`).

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends `cancel_on_pr_close.yml` scheduled-mode `${active_runs_file}` snapshot
Scope-mode justification: The issue asks for one surgical, read-only change, and the plan does exactly that. The `run:` body of "Cancel queued/in-progress runs for closed PR branch" already holds the `actions/runs` snapshot (`${active_runs_file}`, filled by `_cpr_fetch_active_runs`, line ~260). The unlinked count is computed from that file at line 261. The new listing reads the same file with jq, so it adds no GitHub API call (§14) and no new script. Under §20 it is neither a new script nor new scheduler wiring, since it rides the existing five-minute scheduled cleanup. The run-cancel selection (`target_run_ids`), the GraphQL batching (`_cpr_fetch_pr_state_batches`), concurrency and event mode stay untouched. The full version (truncation summary, sanitization, fail-open) costs only a few lines more than a bare listing, so the plan takes it, in line with §6 (Security > Correctness).

### Automation surface (§20.E)
- This change only modifies existing code: one inline step body in `.github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml`. It adds no new script.
- Entry point: the existing scheduled trigger. `internal-cancel-on-pr-close.yml` and the consumer `ai-cancel-on-pr-close.yml` call reusable `cancel_on_pr_close.yml` every 5 minutes; the new code runs only when `EVENT_NAME=schedule`.
- No supervisor, no DB work, and no `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry.

## Files likely to change
- `.github/workflows/cancel_on_pr_close.yml`
- `tests/test_review_merge_train.py`
- `changelog.d/wfopt-0922-3-cancel-cleanup-unlinked-runs.md` (new)

## Functions or modules to implement

**1. In the workflow step "Cancel queued/in-progress runs for closed PR branch"**, inside the existing `if [ "${unlinked_active_run_count}" -gt 0 ]; then` block (lines 262-264):
- Keep the existing line byte-for-byte: `echo "::warning::Scheduled close cleanup preserved ${unlinked_active_run_count} active run(s) without pull-request linkage."`
- Directly after it, add these lines:
  - A short comment naming the issue and the rules: zero API calls, no free-text fields, sanitized values, fail open.
  - A single-quoted shell variable, `unlinked_run_listing_jq='...'`, that holds the jq program. The program must contain no single quote, so a test can extract it with one regex.
  - The call:
    ```
    if ! unlinked_run_listing="$(jq -r --argjson unlinked_run_listing_max 10 "${unlinked_run_listing_jq}" "${active_runs_file}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
      echo "::warning::Scheduled close cleanup could not list the unlinked active run details."
    else
      printf '%s\n' "${unlinked_run_listing}"
    fi
    ```
    `if !` stays safe under `set -euo pipefail`, so a jq failure never aborts the step.

**2. The jq program**, roughly:
```
def _cpr_neutralize: if test("::") then gsub("::"; ": :") | _cpr_neutralize else . end;
def _cpr_safe: (if . == null then "" else tostring end)
  | gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9._/@:+-]"; "_") | _cpr_neutralize | .[0:200];
[.workflow_runs[] | select(((.pull_requests // []) | length) == 0)] as $unlinked
| ($unlinked[0:$unlinked_run_listing_max][]
   | "  unlinked run id=\(.id | _cpr_safe) workflow=\((.path // "") | tostring | sub("@.*$"; "") | _cpr_safe) event=\(.event | _cpr_safe) status=\(.status | _cpr_safe) head_branch=\(.head_branch | _cpr_safe) created_at=\(.created_at | _cpr_safe)"),
  (if ($unlinked | length) > $unlinked_run_listing_max
   then "  ... \(($unlinked | length) - $unlinked_run_listing_max) more unlinked active run(s) not listed."
   else empty end)
```
- It uses the same unlinked predicate as the count on line 261, so the listing and the count can never disagree.
- The recursive `_cpr_neutralize` exists because a single `gsub` turns `:::` into `: ::`. Looping until no `::` remains guarantees no adjacent colons.
- Order of operations: character filter, then neutralise, then cap at 200 characters. Truncation cannot create a new `::`.
- Every line starts with two spaces, so it is plain log output and never a workflow command.
- The program reads only `id`, `path`, `event`, `status`, `head_branch` and `created_at`. It never reads `display_title`, `name`, `head_commit` or any other free-text field.

**3. Test in `tests/test_review_merge_train.py`** (append-only, new function at the end of the file): `test_scheduled_cancel_sweep_lists_unlinked_runs_safely`. It uses a local `import re, shutil` inside the function so the module header stays untouched.
- **Contract part (always runs):**
  - the existing warning line still exists verbatim;
  - the workflow contains `--argjson unlinked_run_listing_max 10`, `"${active_runs_file}"` next to the listing, and the fail-open warning text;
  - the listing block does not contain `display_title` or `.name`.
- **Behaviour part:** `pytest.skip` when `shutil.which("jq") is None`, following the `tests/test_activation_verify.py:587` pattern.
  - Extract the program with `re.search(r"unlinked_run_listing_jq='(.*?)'\n", workflow, re.S)`.
  - Write a fixture runs file with:
    - 2 linked runs (`pull_requests: [{"number": 5}]`) with distinctive IDs;
    - 13 unlinked runs (`pull_requests: []`, plus one with the key missing);
    - one unlinked run whose `head_branch` is `"x\n::error::pwned\u0007:::y"`;
    - one unlinked run whose `head_branch` is 500 characters long;
    - one unlinked run whose path is `owner/repo/.github/workflows/x.yml@refs/heads/main`;
    - a `display_title` of `SECRET_TITLE_MARKER` on every run.
  - Run `jq -r --argjson unlinked_run_listing_max 10 <program> <file>` through `subprocess.run`.
  - Assert:
    - exactly 11 output lines, the last being `... 3 more unlinked active run(s) not listed.`;
    - the linked run IDs are absent;
    - `SECRET_TITLE_MARKER` is absent;
    - no line contains `::`;
    - no control characters appear;
    - the `@refs/heads/main` suffix is stripped;
    - no value is longer than 200 characters.

**4. Changelog fragment** `changelog.d/wfopt-0922-3-cancel-cleanup-unlinked-runs.md`:
- marker `<!-- changelog: changed -->`;
- a bold one-sentence summary plus a short paragraph in §20 voice: before/after, zero new API calls, the up-to-10 cap, sanitized fields and fail-open, and what it means for operators.

## Data structures affected
None. The program reads the existing `actions/runs` JSON (`workflow_runs[]`) and writes nothing.

## API or interface changes
- No new GitHub API calls, inputs, outputs, env vars or wrapper changes.
- New log output: plain lines `  unlinked run id=… workflow=… event=… status=… head_branch=… created_at=…`, an optional summary line, and an optional `::warning::` when the listing fails.
- New shell names `unlinked_run_listing_jq` and `unlinked_run_listing`, plus jq names `_cpr_neutralize`, `_cpr_safe` and `$unlinked_run_listing_max`. A grep found only `unlinked_active_run_count` among `unlinked_*` names in this step, so none of the new names clash.

## Decisions

### D1 — Hold the jq program in a single-quoted shell variable
- **Chosen:** `unlinked_run_listing_jq='…'`, passed to `jq -r`.
- **Alternatives considered:** an inline `jq -r '…'` like the neighbouring calls; a new script under `scripts/`.
- **Why:** the test can extract the exact program and run it on a fixture, so the test checks the shipped code rather than a copy. A new script would need staging and wiring for a few lines of logic.

### D2 — Neutralise `::` by repeating until none remain
- **Chosen:** a recursive `gsub` (`_cpr_neutralize`).
- **Alternatives considered:** one `gsub("::"; ": :")`.
- **Why:** a single pass leaves `: ::` for `:::`, which breaks the "no `::` in any value" requirement.

### D3 — Print plain lines with a two-space indent, not annotations
- **Chosen:** `printf '%s\n'` of the jq output.
- **Alternatives considered:** one `::notice::` per run.
- **Why:** the issue asks for non-annotation lines. Indented lines can never be read as workflow commands, and they avoid filling the annotation list.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary:** `head_branch` and `path` come from runs that PR authors and forks can create (fork `pull_request` runs appear in the snapshot). They are untrusted text that reaches the Actions log. Mitigations:
  - allowlist character filter (control characters and newlines become `_`);
  - `::` neutralised, plus a leading indent on every line;
  - 200-character cap per value;
  - free-text fields (`display_title`, `name`) never read.
- **No authorization surface:** the change is read-only and makes no new token use or API call. It handles no secrets; IDs, refs and timestamps are not sensitive.
- **Abuse cases covered:**
  - a branch named `::error::…` or `::add-mask::…`;
  - a newline-injected second command;
  - a very long branch name flooding the log;
  - a hostile run title (not printed at all).

## Potential risks or edge cases
- **jq not installed or malformed JSON:** the existing count on line 261 would already fail first (unchanged behaviour). The listing's own failure is fail-open.
- **`null` fields:** these print as empty values.
- **Reusable-workflow `path` with `@refs/...`:** the suffix is stripped before sanitising, because `@` is an allowed character.
- **Workflow size:** about 18.8 KB, far below the §24 guard.
- **CI sharding:** `tests/test_review_merge_train.py` runs in 3 local CI shards. A new test function needs no CI change.
- No conflicts found between the issue and the codebase. Line numbers, the warning text and the test location (`test_scheduled_cancel_sweep_batches_live_pr_state_and_fails_safe`, around line 1857) all match.

Failure modes:
- **Listing jq fails.** Symptom: `::warning::Scheduled close cle
